sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander. 2020. Plurality marking in Leko and Yendang groups (Adamawa, Niger-Congo) with some reference to noun classification. Language in Africa 1(3): 125-154.

sources.citation: Anikina, Tatiana, Anastasia Lyakhovich & Alexander Zheltov. 2016 [file created Sept 2012]. Towards a comparative description of the Adamawa languages of Mumuye-Yendang and Leko groups. Slides (.ppt, 2,142 words), Proto-Niger-Congo 2 congress, Paris. Yendang data from T. Anikina's 2012 fieldwork.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sections are classification, lexicostatistics (Yendang/Wakka 75%), plural marking, pronouns, numerals, copulas, kinship. Yendang forms carry tone marks (wɛ̀ŋ, lɛ̀ŋ, birɛ̀ŋ) but no statement on tone or stress; a full-text search for stress/accent/phonol returns nothing relevant.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; an administrative code-split request (intelligibility test, lexical similarity 13% Yotti-Yendang, village counts). It is the only Glottolog reference for yend1240.
